whatIsWebDev.title: What is Web Development?
whatIsWebDev.description: Web development is building applications, services, or sites that run over the web, whether that's consumer-facing websites or backend enterprise systems delivered through web technologies. It can range from creating simple informational pages to developing complex APIs and client-server systems that power entire organizations. At its core, web development is about using the web as the platform for delivering software and connecting people with the tools or information they need.

frontend.title: Frontend Development
frontend.description: Frontend web development is about creating the part of a website or app that people directly use. It shapes how users see, click, type, and move through the interface. Ultimately, it bridges design and user experience into a functional product.

backend.title: Backend Development
backend.description: Backend web development is about building the logic, infrastructure, and systems that support a digital product. It handles how data is stored, processed, and shared between different parts of the application. Ultimately, it enables the product to function as an interconnected, intelligent system.

approach.title: My Approach
approach.description: For me, great engineering isn't just about code or metrics, it's about trust. When a client hands you a complex problem, they're trusting that you can deliver value. They rely on you not just to write solutions, but to understand their needs, anticipate risks, and communicate with clarity. Engineering, at its best, is a partnership, where every line of code reflects reliability, every decision reflects integrity, and every outcome strengthens that trust.

why.title: Why Your Business Needs Professional Web Development
paragraphs: Your website is often the first place people encounter your brand it's your digital storefront. In just a few seconds, visitors decide whether to stay and explore or click away. That's why design and usability are critical. A skilled web developer can craft a layout that captures attention and keeps users engaged.

One of the biggest benefits of working with a professional web developer is the chance to build a site that truly reflects your business. Unlike cookie-cutter website builders, custom development gives you freedom. Your website can align perfectly with your brand voice, whether you want something bold and creative or simple and minimalist.

support.title: Support and Maintenance
support.description: A website needs regular updates to stay secure and effective. Ongoing support ensures your site runs smoothly and grows with your business.

ux.title: Improved User Experience
ux.description: Easy navigation, fast loading, and clear design keep visitors engaged and more likely to convert into customers.

responsive.title: Responsiveness
responsive.description: A responsive site adapts to any device, giving users a smooth experience on mobile, tablet, or desktop.

hero.title: Who is a Web Developer?
hero.subtitle: A web developer builds the digital layer of today’s world, turning ideas into websites, apps, and online tools people use every day.

what.title: What Does a Web Developer Do?
what.description: A web developer creates websites and applications that run on the internet. Frontend is what you see and use, backend runs in the background—together, they make the web work.
what.imageAlt: Frontend (a browser window with interface elements) connected to backend (servers and databases)

frontend.title: Frontend web developer: what the user sees
frontend.description: Frontend developers work on the interface. They make sure everything looks right, loads fast, and reacts when you click or type.

backend.title: Backend web developer: the logic behind the scenes
backend.description: Backend developers work on the hidden logic. They handle data, security, servers, and everything that makes the system run reliably.

skills.title: Skills That Shape a Web Developer
skills.description: A good developer doesn’t just know code—they understand how people use the web and how businesses grow online.

items.title: Problem solving in web development
items.description: Breaking down complex issues and finding working solutions.

items.title: Design awareness for better user experience
items.description: Knowing how design choices affect usability and flow.

items.title: Technical adaptability: frameworks and web standards
items.description: Staying current with frameworks, languages, and web standards.

items.title: Collaboration with designers, clients and developers
items.description: Working with designers, clients, and developers.

items.title: User focus in every website
items.description: Always building with the end-user’s experience in mind.

why.title: Why Web Developers Matter
paragraphs: Every brand needs a digital presence, and a website is often the first step. Without one, you’re invisible to most of your audience.
A skilled web developer helps create tools that don’t just exist—they perform: better reach, more engagement, stronger trust.

points.title: First impressions: a website that keeps visitors
points.description: Opinions form in seconds. Good development keeps visitors engaged.

points.title: A scalable website that grows with your business
points.description: A strong foundation lets your site or app grow with your business.

points.title: A reliable website with minimal downtime
points.description: Secure, stable, well-maintained systems prevent downtime and protect your data.

technologies.title: Technologies a Modern Web Developer Uses
technologies.intro: My most-used technologies as a web developer in Oslo, where full-stack development covers both frontend and backend.

items.title: React: reusable components
items.description: A JavaScript library for interfaces built from reusable components.

items.title: Next.js: fast, search-friendly pages
items.description: Builds on React with server rendering and routing. Pages load fast and are easy for Google to read.

items.title: WordPress: a proven publishing tool
items.description: Powers a large share of the world's websites. Fits when editors want to update content themselves.

items.title: Sanity: headless CMS for structured content
items.description: Separates content from presentation, so it can be shown on a website, an app, or other channels.

items.title: Node.js: JavaScript on the server
items.description: Backend, APIs, and integrations in the same language as the frontend.

become.title: How Do You Become a Web Developer?
become.intro: There is no single path in: a degree, vocational college, a course, or self-study. Employers want to see what you can show.

steps.title: Learn the foundation: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript
steps.description: Everything on the web builds on these three. Learn them well before frameworks.

steps.title: Pick one framework and go deep
steps.description: React is among the most requested skills in job listings; Next.js is a short step from there.

steps.title: Build a portfolio of your own projects
steps.description: Real projects say more than a diploma. Build a site for a friend and publish the code on GitHub.

steps.title: Learn Git and teamwork
steps.description: Version control, code review, and working with designers matter as much as coding.

steps.title: Apply for junior roles or take small gigs
steps.description: Junior roles, trainee programs, and small freelance gigs give experience. The key is to start.

become.outro: I have worked as a web developer since 2004 and still learn something new every week.

employment.title: Freelancer, Consultant, or Employee?
employment.intro: Web development can be bought in different ways. What fits depends on project, budget, and timeframe.

options.title: Freelance web developer: flexible and direct
options.description: A freelancer works on their own account. You get direct contact and often lower costs than at a large agency.

options.title: Consultant: broad experience from many projects
options.description: A consultant is employed by a consultancy and hired out to clients. I consult at OsloWeb AS, delivering for municipalities and tech companies.

options.title: In-house web developer: long-term ownership
options.description: An in-house developer knows the product in depth, which pays off long-term.

price.title: How Much Does a Web Developer Cost?
price.intro: Price depends on scope, complexity, and who you hire. These are approximate Norwegian price levels, excluding VAT, not a quote.

ranges.title: Hourly rate for a web developer
ranges.description: Freelancers are often lower, agencies higher.

ranges.title: Simple business website
ranges.description: A presentation site with a few subpages, a contact form, and a publishing tool such as WordPress.

ranges.title: Custom web development
ranges.range: typically from approx. NOK 50,000 and up
ranges.description: Web applications, online stores, and integrations require more planning and testing.

price.note: Remember ongoing costs for hosting, domain, licenses, and maintenance. Ask for a written estimate.

choose.title: How to Choose the Right Web Developer
choose.intro: Whether you want web developers near me or a web developer in Oslo, a few questions separate the good from the rest.

tips.title: Look at previous projects
tips.description: Ask for examples of sites the developer has built. Check that they load fast and work on mobile.

tips.title: Ask why, not just what
tips.description: A good web developer explains why a technology suits you, not just what they prefer.

tips.title: Clarify ownership and maintenance
tips.description: Make sure you own the code, domain, and content, and that updates are planned.

tips.title: Judge the communication
tips.description: Clear, quick answers before you sign are a good sign.

choose.outro: Being local helps. A web developer near you can meet face to face and is easy to reach when something is urgent.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions about web developers

items.question: What does a web developer do?
items.answer: A web developer builds and maintains websites and web solutions, from what visitors see (frontend) to the servers, databases and logic behind it (backend).

items.question: What is the difference between frontend and backend?
items.answer: Frontend is what users see and use: layout, buttons and forms. Backend is behind the scenes: data storage, login and integrations.

items.question: How much does it cost to hire a web developer?
items.answer: Hourly rates in Norway are often around NOK 800–1,500 excl. VAT, depending on experience and whether you hire a freelancer or an agency. A simple business website typically starts around NOK 15,000; larger solutions cost more.

items.question: What skills does a web developer need?
items.answer: The core is HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Many also use React and Next.js, and databases, APIs, version control, performance and accessibility matter.

items.question: How do I choose the right web developer?
items.answer: Look at previous projects, ask why a technology suits you, clarify ownership of code and domain, and judge how clearly the developer communicates.

items.question: Do you work as a web developer in Oslo?
items.answer: Yes, Majid Askarifarsangi is a web developer in Oslo and works with clients locally and nationwide. Get in touch for a no-obligation chat.

what.title: What Is Modern Web Development?
what.description: In business, web development turns commercial goals and workflows into reliable browser software. Where traditional website development meant static pages, modern projects span editorial CMS platforms, customer portals, and web application development. Building a durable product requires visual identity, content structure, accessibility, and search visibility to work with code and infrastructure.
what.imageAlt: Diagram of browser client connected to APIs, CMS, and server logic

frontend.title: The Client and Interface Layer (Frontend)
frontend.description: The client layer is the interactive surface on the user's device. Across frontend and backend development, it ensures responsive layouts, fast transitions, keyboard accessibility, and instant feedback when visitors submit forms or filter data.

backend.title: Server Logic, APIs, and Data Storage (Backend)
backend.description: Behind the interface sits the architecture governing business logic, authentication, databases, and data flows. Through structured APIs, the solution connects securely to CMS platforms, payments, or external systems so the service runs reliably.

process.title: How a Web Development Project Runs – Step by Step
process.intro: A structured web development process reduces risk, keeps budgets predictable, and ensures the product supports business goals. From sketch to production, delivery follows five stages:

steps.title: 1. Discovery, Goals, and Technical Architecture
steps.description: We map audiences, business goals, functional requirements, and integrations, assess feasibility, and prepare estimates.

steps.title: 2. Structure, User Experience, and UI Design in Figma
steps.description: Information architecture and user journeys are outlined before building interactive Figma prototypes, validating flows before coding.

steps.title: 3. Frontend, Backend, and Integration Development
steps.description: Designs become modular components—often documented in Storybook—while CMS, data schemas, and API integrations are built under version control.

steps.title: 4. Performance, Accessibility (WCAG), and Technical SEO
steps.description: Before launch, the solution is verified for Core Web Vitals, mobile speed, semantic HTML, WCAG compliance, and search metadata.

steps.title: 5. Launch, Analytics, and Ongoing Maintenance
steps.description: The site is deployed to cloud infrastructure with SSL and analytics, followed by editor training, security updates, and improvements.

process.outro: Clear milestones and short decision loops give full visibility throughout the project.

technologies.title: Choosing the Right Technology and Platform in Web Development
technologies.intro: Technology choices should be driven by business needs, editorial workflow, and integrations rather than trends.

items.title: Next.js and React for Custom, High-Speed Solutions
items.description: When a project demands custom web development, interactivity, or tailored logic, React and Next.js deliver server rendering, top speed, and strong technical SEO.

items.title: Sanity (Headless CMS) for Structured Multi-Channel Content
items.description: Sanity decouples content storage from presentation, fitting organizations wanting a tailored studio and reusable structured content across channels.

items.title: WordPress for Flexible, Proven Publishing
items.description: A well-built WordPress site with a custom theme gives editors a familiar, cost-effective publishing tool for company sites, news, and landing pages.

items.title: TypeScript, Node.js, and Modern API Architecture
items.description: Type safety with TypeScript, Node.js services (Express.js or Nest.js), and PostgreSQL databases provide dependable integrations and maintainable code.

items.title: Cloud Hosting, Core Web Vitals, and Security
items.description: Deploying on Netlify or Vercel with a global CDN ensures low latency, high uptime, and strong Core Web Vitals scores.

price.title: How Much Does Web Development Cost in Norway?
price.intro: When evaluating web development cost or website cost in Norway, pricing depends on scope, design, and integrations. The tiers below show typical, approximate Norwegian ranges (excl. VAT) as guidance, not quotes:

ranges.title: Business Website with a CMS
ranges.description: Typical for a company website with responsive design, contact forms, technical SEO, and a CMS like WordPress or Sanity.

ranges.title: Custom Web Application and Integrations
ranges.range: typically from approx. NOK 50,000 excl. VAT and up
ranges.description: Covers larger deliveries with custom React and Next.js interfaces, authentication, dashboards, databases, or API integrations.

ranges.title: Hourly Consulting and Ongoing Development
ranges.description: Suited for ongoing development, performance optimization, code reviews, or embedding senior engineering capacity into a team.

price.note: Cost drivers like content migration, WCAG compliance, and recurring fees for domain, hosting, and maintenance should be clarified in a written estimate.

choose.title: Web Agency or Senior Consultant – Which Should You Choose?
choose.intro: Choosing between a web agency vs. consultant shapes budget, speed, and proximity to problem solving. Large agencies suit big campaigns, while a consultant via OsloWeb AS gives direct access to senior engineering without agency overhead.

tips.title: Direct Dialogue with the Engineer Building Your Solution
tips.description: Working directly with the consultant who designs the architecture and writes the code prevents misunderstandings and speeds up decisions.

tips.title: The Right Technology for Your Needs – Not Cookie-Cutter Templates
tips.description: An independent consultant objectively evaluates whether WordPress, Sanity, or custom Next.js best fits your workflow and budget.

tips.title: Full Ownership of Source Code, Domain, and Content
tips.description: Transparent agreements ensure your business retains full control of your Git code, domain, CMS, and data without vendor lock-in.

tips.title: Predictable Operations, Performance, and Long-Term Support
tips.description: Partnering with a consultant in Oslo ensures continuity across security updates, SEO improvements, and new features.

choose.outro: Ask for reference projects, clear milestones, and an honest assessment of business value.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions About Web Development

items.question: What does professional web development involve?
items.answer: It covers planning, designing, coding, testing, and operating websites or web applications—from the browser interface (frontend) to server logic, APIs, security, and technical SEO (backend).

items.question: How long does it take to develop a new website?
items.answer: A business website with a CMS typically takes 3–6 weeks from discovery and Figma design to launch. Custom web applications and integrations usually take 6 weeks to several months.

items.question: How much does web development cost for a business in Norway?
items.answer: A company website with a CMS often costs around NOK 15,000–50,000 excl. VAT, while custom web applications typically start from approx. NOK 50,000 and up. Hourly consulting rates are normally approx. NOK 800–1,500 excl. VAT.

items.question: Should we choose WordPress, Sanity, or custom Next.js?
items.answer: WordPress fits content-driven sites wanting a familiar editor. Sanity with Next.js excels for high performance and structured multi-channel content, while custom React/Next.js suits web applications.

items.question: Why are accessibility (WCAG) and Core Web Vitals important?
items.answer: Norwegian businesses must meet WCAG standards so sites work for everyone. Meanwhile, Core Web Vitals measure speed and stability, affecting usability, conversions, and search rankings.

items.question: What is the advantage of choosing a consultant over a large web agency?
items.answer: You work directly with the senior developer building your solution, avoid agency overhead, and move faster from idea to production.

items.question: Do you offer web development and consulting in the Oslo area?
items.answer: Yes, I am based in Sandvika/Oslo and deliver web development, UI/UX design, and consulting via OsloWeb AS for clients across Oslo, Bærum, and Norway.
